note: Every number here is copied directly from DARPAN's own recorded test results, not recomputed or estimated for this corpus. See content/03-ml-and-detection.md for the full explanation of each figure.

physicsBaseline.measuredOver: ~4 hours of simulated healthy flight (14,404 samples) plus injected-fault test missions

rulCoverage.acceptanceBar: true crossing time falls inside the P10-P90 band in >= 80% of runs

detectorComparison.heldOutOn: every high-altitude mission profile — excluded entirely from training, so this is a held-out operating regime, not just held-out samples

ablationStudy.purpose: Checks whether the ML model's advantage is real, or whether it's just re-reading features the physics detector already computes.
ablationStudy.keyFinding: The model trained on raw residual statistics ALONE (49 features, none derived from the physics detector's own reasoning) still catches 45 of 54 — close to the full-feature model. This shows the model is learning something real from the data, not repackaging the physics detector's own verdict.
ablationStudy.honestNegativeFinding: Adding hand-engineered component-coupling features very mildly HURTS detection count (48 -> 47) for essentially no change in severity (0.109 -> 0.110). Reported as 'no measurable help' rather than dropped from the writeup.

trainableFaultCoverage.reason: Bottlenecked by the frozen sensor suite, not by missing labels — most untrainable faults need a channel (spectral vibration, knock, propeller-shaft rpm) the modeled instrument suite does not carry at all.
trainableFaultCoverage.oneKnownPathToTwelfth: One additional fault already has everything else needed (a real root-factor coupling) and is blocked only on an incident-class assignment plus a deliberate retrain decision — not taken automatically as a side effect of unrelated work.
